title: Existence of representing measures for finite-dimensional function spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a topological space, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space of continuous real-valued functions on $S$, let $V^*$ be its dual, and assume $Z(V)=\varnothing$. Given $L\in V^*$, does there exist a positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $S$ such that
$$
L(f)=\int_S f\,d\mu\qquad\text{for every }f\in V?
$$
completeness_reason: Z(V) is undefined in the literal; interpreting it as common zero set restores a precise but trivial universal reading.
technical_assessment: For singleton S and V=span(1), L(1)=-1 has no positive measure. Source pp60-61 defines Z, M and C, gives a positivity cone and starts a core-variety characterization. The literal turns a characterization problem into universal existence; no discovery credit.

title: Bárány–Kalai–Meshulam connectivity conjecture for deleted joins of matroids
statement: **Conjecture 1 (Bárány, Kalai, and Meshulam, 2016).** For any integer $k \ge 1$ there exists an integer $n_k \ge 1$ depending only on $k$ such that for any matroid $M$ of rank $r \ge 1$ with at least $n_k$ disjoint bases, the $k$-fold deleted join $M^{*k}_{\Delta}$ of the matroid $M$ is $(kr-1)$-dimensional and $(kr-2)$-connected.
completeness_reason: For every k an n_k independent of rank and all matroids with enough disjoint bases are specified.
technical_assessment: Connectivity in every degree up to kr-2 is stronger than a dimension count or Euler characteristic. Disjoint bases yield full-dimensional faces but no complete high-connectivity mechanism.

title: Conjecture on transversals for line families with the $(p,3)$-property
statement: Suppose $p\ge 3$ is an integer and a family of straight lines $\mathcal F$ has the $(p,3)$-property. Then there exists a point set $U$ such that $|U|\le p-2$ and $\ell\cap U\ne\varnothing$ for all lines $\ell\in\mathcal F$.

technical_assessment: Under a planar concurrence interpretation the conclusion is a p-2 piercing bound; higher-dimensional skew lines change the setting. No eligible counterexample without source scope.

title: Homological Sperner-type theorem for rainbow simplices
statement: Let $K$ be a simplicial complex whose vertices are painted with the colors $I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. title: Upper bound for totally mixed facets of Minkowski sums of triangles
statement: For every integer $d\ge 2$, let $P_0,\ldots,P_{d-2}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be triangles whose Minkowski sum $P_0+\cdots+P_{d-2}$ is full-dimensional. Then the number of totally mixed facets of $P_0+\cdots+P_{d-2}$—facets expressible as $F_0+\cdots+F_{d-2}$ with each $F_i$ an edge of $P_i$—is at most $1+2^{d-1}$.
completeness_reason: All d>=2, full-dimensional sums and the exact meaning of totally mixed facets are explicit.
technical_assessment: Facet counts require simultaneous compatible edge normal cones; counting all 3^(d-1) edge choices gives a weaker bound than 1+2^(d-1). No sharp global combinatorial bound found.

title: Sobolev sheaves on subanalytic sites for $s\geq \tfrac12$
statement: Let $M$ be a real analytic manifold and let $s\geq \tfrac12$. Does there exist a complex $H^s$ of sheaves, defined in the derived category of sheaves in the subanalytic Grothendieck topology on $M$, such that, for every relatively compact open Lipschitz subset $U\subset M$, $H^s(U)$ coincides with the complex concentrated in degree $0$ and equal to the classical Sobolev space $H^s(U)$?
completeness_reason: Every analytic manifold, s>=1/2 and every relatively compact Lipschitz open have an explicit derived restriction requirement.
technical_assessment: A naive sheaf of Sobolev sections need not have derived acyclicity on all Lipschitz opens. Partitions of unity alone do not verify the requested higher-cohomology vanishing; no full construction.
